rationale: Revise the multi-requester experiment so each requester has its own result event. The previous run reported the earliest request answered with the newest context and left at index zero, and the middle request likewise, but the shared event names left those comparisons marked incomplete and the newest-read prediction unresolved. The harness now emits read_a_reply, read_b_reply, read_c_reply and read_a_completion, read_b_completion, read_c_completion, so each comparison's admission is unambiguous; no production code or scheduling input changes.

experiment.revision_reason: Emit one result event per requester (read_a_reply, read_b_reply, read_c_reply and their completion states) so each comparison correlates to its own admission; the earlier version reused one event name for three requesters, which left the comparisons incomplete and the newest-read prediction unresolved.

scope.description: Three remote reads, one confirmation. Node 2 queues two reads and node 3 queues one between them; one leader tick makes the periodic heartbeat carry the newest context, and the replies plus the completion state of all three admitted reads are measured.
assumptions: The voter group is three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3}; node 1 is leader and each node uses a test-only in-memory ILogDB.
All three reads are registered through the node-level pendingReadIndex and forwarded through the real follower path, in the order read-A from node 2, read-B from node 3 and read-C from node 2.
The only scheduling input is one leader tick, and the harness delivers only the heartbeat addressed to node 3; it does not choose which read is confirmed.

Each requester's reply and completion state is emitted as its own event, so a comparison is correlated only to that requester's admission even though the two replies addressed to node 2 carry identical contexts and indexes.
excluded: No NodeHost, transport, persistence, restart or snapshot path is exercised.
No proposal or membership change is made while the reads are outstanding.
The run observes reply-context association and pending-read completion only; it does not attempt to establish a stale data value.

experiment.prefix: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed. It registers a pending read on node 2 and forwards it, then registers one on node 3 and forwards it, then registers a second read on node 2 and forwards that, so the leader's queue holds three remote requests in that order. It calls Tick once on the leader and pumps it; the produced heartbeat addressed to node 3 carries the newest queued context. That heartbeat is delivered to node 3, its echo is returned to the leader, and the leader's replies are collected and grouped by address. The replies for node 2 and the reply for node 3 are emitted with their response contexts and indexes, then delivered to their nodes; the resulting ReadyToRead output and the confirmed index are fed to each node's pendingReadIndex, and the run records for each admitted read whether its batch still exists, its index and whether it completed.
experiment.requirement: When one confirmation returns several earlier remote requests, each requester must receive a result tagged with its own SystemCtx and every admitted read must complete once the confirmed index is applied.
experiment.responsibility: readIndex.confirm returns the queued requests up to the confirmed context, and handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation builds each remote reply from the confirming heartbeat's context; the requesting nodes' pendingReadIndex consume those replies. The experiment exercises those real handlers and changes only how many reads are queued and which node issues them.

comparisons.description: The earliest queued request must be answered with its own context.
The earliest queued read must complete after the confirmed index is applied.
The middle queued read must also complete after the same confirmed index is applied.
The newest queued read, whose context confirmed the batch, must complete.
